title: Reading a distance-time graph: the slope is the speed
examples: How do you find speed from a distance-time graph?
What does a flat line mean on a distance-time graph?
What does a steep line mean?

marks.label: 10 min, 3 km
marks.ask: How do you find speed from a distance-time graph?

explain.say: Kofi cycles from home in Accra to his football practice. This graph tells his story. Time goes along the bottom, distance from home goes up the side. Look at the start: 0 minutes, 0 kilometres.

draw.text: Reading a distance-time graph: the slope is the speed

marks.label: 10 min, 3 km
marks.ask: How do you find speed from a distance-time graph?

explain.say: After 10 minutes, Kofi is 3 kilometres from home. See the dot? So he goes 3 kilometres every 10 minutes. How far will he be after 20 minutes?

marks.label: 10 min, 3 km
marks.ask: How do you find speed from a distance-time graph?

explain.say: 6 kilometres! The slope of the line, the gradient, is his speed: 6 kilometres in 20 minutes is 0.3 kilometres a minute. Times 60 gives 18 kilometres an hour.

marks.label: 10 min, 3 km
marks.ask: How do you find speed from a distance-time graph?

explain.say: Now look at the three kinds of line. Steep means fast. Gentle means slow. And a flat line means the distance is not changing, so Kofi has stopped, maybe at a traffic light. Which line is a rest?

groups.label: Steep line
groups.ask: What does a steeper line mean?

groups.label: Flat line
groups.ask: What does a flat line on a distance-time graph mean?

explain.say: The flat one! Well done. Here is Kofi next to a walker and a bus. Wow: a steeper line on the graph always means a taller speed bar here. Challenge: if a line goes up 12 kilometres in 1 hour, what is the speed?

faq.q: How do you find speed from a distance-time graph?
faq.a: Find the gradient: distance gone divided by time taken. 6 kilometres in 20 minutes is 0.3 kilometres a minute.
asks: What does the slope of a distance-time graph show?

faq.q: What does a flat line on a distance-time graph mean?
faq.a: The distance is not changing, so the person is not moving. They have stopped.

faq.q: What does a steeper line mean?
faq.a: A steeper line means more distance in the same time, so a faster speed.
asks: Steep line on a distance-time graph

faq.q: How do you change kilometres per minute to kilometres per hour?
faq.a: Multiply by 60, because an hour has 60 minutes. 0.3 kilometres a minute is 18 kilometres an hour.
asks: Convert km per minute to km per hour

faq.q: What does a line going down mean?
faq.a: The distance from home is getting smaller, so the person is coming back home.
asks: Why does a distance-time graph go down?

facts: On a distance-time graph, the gradient equals the speed.
A horizontal line on a distance-time graph means the object is stationary.

quiz.say: A line on a distance-time graph goes from 0 to 10 kilometres in 2 hours. What is the speed?
quiz.why: Speed is distance divided by time: 10 divided by 2 is 5 kilometres per hour.

quiz.say: What does a flat section on a distance-time graph show?
quiz.why: The distance stays the same, so the person is still.

wrong.1: Fast movement is a steep line.
wrong.2: Going back home is a line sloping down.
